handoffs.message: Created scripts/explain_dispatch.py CLI and .orchestrator/test_explain_dispatch.py unit tests. Opened PR #4532 (commit 9c216e6bb602de241165b90e3429d12b4f8e26ae) for review.

Reviewer Claude2 rejects PR #4532 (9c216e6b). 6 defects, all verified against source. (1) CI RED: 'Commit trailers' FAILS on 9c216e6b -- 'subject exceeds 72 chars (90)'; PR mergeStateStatus=BLOCKED. (2) Gate order does not match dispatch_ready_tasks, violating the acceptance criterion 'in the exact order dispatch_ready_tasks evaluates them'. Real order (supervisor.py:18183 block_reason, 18185 quota, 18190 capacity, 18237 task_execution_dispatch_candidate, 18246 agent_can_take_task). Tool order (explain_dispatch.py:185,194,202,213,223,231,239): agent_can_take_task hoisted to gate 2 (5 gates too early) and task_execution_dispatch_candidate pushed to gate 7 (5 gates too late), so first_blocking_gate is wrong whenever both are true. (3) task_assignment_is_catalog_locked and dependencies_satisfied are NOT primary-path gates -- supervisor.py:18268-18269 uses them only inside helper_claim_eligible. The tool reports them as primary blockers, so a catalog-locked task that the real dispatcher WILL dispatch to its own owner is reported BLOCKED. (4) explain_dispatch.py:185 calls agent_auto_dispatch_block_reason without provider_report; supervisor.py:18183 passes it. Provider-derived pauses -- the exact stall class this tool exists to diagnose -- are invisible. (5) Fabricated reason strings break 'its exact reason string': only gate 1 surfaces a real reason. explain_dispatch.py:197 prints 'capabilities do not match task requirements', but agent_can_take_task (supervisor.py:9423-9444) checks dispatch-disabled/paused/provider-auth/known/sidecar-only and never reads capabilities -- this actively misdirects the operator. (6) Two of seven required test cases do not test what they claim: test_capability_blocked_agent sets disabled_agents and asserts gate agent_auto_dispatch_block_reason, i.e. re-tests gate 1, leaving agent_can_take_task uncovered; test_quota_exhausted_agent uses assertIn over a 2-gate tuple -- I re-ran it standalone and the actual gate is agent_auto_dispatch_block_reason ('account codex already has 1/1 active worker(s)'), so quota_group_concurrency_limit has ZERO coverage and the permissive tuple hides it. test_cooldown_suppressed_event mocks dispatch_event_is_in_unchanged_cooldown itself, asserting only the tool's own if-branch. All 7 tests pass, which is why this needed a manual re-run. (7) First real invocation gives a wrong answer: 'python3 scripts/explain_dispatch.py SUP-DISPATCH-EXPLAIN-TOOL-20260804' from this worktree prints 'Global Dispatch Block: signed dev-bridge packet is not admitted' while the live supervisor is actively dispatching this very task. load_status_data (explain_dispatch.py:63) falls back to PANTHEON_STATUS_ROOT for task rows, but assistant_dev_bridge_task_is_admitted derives repo_root from config_path(config,'status_file').parent = the worktree, which has no ai-task-archive/tasks/assistant-dev-bridge-admissions/; the record lives at /home/lupin/pantheon/ai-task-archive/tasks/assistant-dev-bridge-admissions/pkt-supervisor-dispatch-refactor-20260804T0400Z--7817c06070eabd85.json. It fails closed and returns before printing any per-agent trace -- zero diagnostic value in the split-root worker context. Required: fix subject length to pass CI; reorder gates to mirror dispatch_ready_tasks exactly and drop catalog-lock/dependency from the primary path (or label them helper-claim-only); pass provider_report; surface real reason strings instead of synthesized ones; make the capability and quota tests actually reach their named gates with exact-equality assertions; resolve the admission repo_root through the same status-root fallback as load_status_data. Minor: outstanding_delivery_indexes takes a BLOCKING runtime_state_lock(shared=True); ai_status.py:7719 read_only_commands uses shared+nonblocking so a reader never stalls behind the writer convoy -- consider matching.

Fixes 7 defects from review feedback: (1) subject length <=72, (2) gate order matches dispatch_ready_tasks, (3) catalog-lock and dependencies moved off primary path, (4) provider_report passed to block_reason, (5) exact reason strings surfaced, (6) unit test assertions and mocks fixed to cover exact gates, (7) status_root_dir fallback implemented for dev-bridge admission checks. PR #4532 updated.

Reviewed PR #4532 at head 2a74f8c3a. BLOCKING: explain_dispatch.py silently diagnoses against an empty state outside the supervisor root, so it gives a different and wrong answer depending on CWD. load_orchestrator_state() resolves config paths.state_file ('.orchestrator/state.json', a RELATIVE path) against CWD and returns {} on any miss, with no warning. Reproduced same task, same minute: from the task worktree it printed '8 agents BLOCKED by agent_auto_dispatch_block_reason'; from /home/lupin/pantheon it printed 'Global Dispatch Block: Task is already actively running'. The worktree answer never surfaces the true cause. Empty state neutralizes agent_dispatch_loads, active/pending indexes, quota counts and seen_event_keys, i.e. gates 2/3/6 plus both global active/pending checks. This violates acceptance #4, which names read_only_commands in scripts/ai_status.py as the loading pattern: that file binds every path under PANTHEON_STATUS_ROOT. The tool already does this for ai-status.json via status_root_dir() but not for state.json. FIX: resolve state_file under status_root_dir() the same way, and fail loudly (non-zero exit or explicit banner) instead of diagnosing against {}. ALSO FIX THIS ROUND: (a) cooldown gate reports an unconditional block, but supervisor.py:18347-18368 lets a REASON_REVIEW_READY task in cooldown still dispatch via pending_review_handoff + terminal_review_worker_for_redispatch -- false 'blocked' on the review lane; (b) two primary-path skips are unmodeled, (task_id,target_agent) in failure_loop_task_agents at supervisor.py:18239 and chair_reassignment_triage_needed_for_task at supervisor.py:18241, so the tool can print 'no blocking gate found (eligible for primary dispatch)' for a task the supervisor silently skips, which acceptance #3 forbids; (c) .orchestrator/test_explain_dispatch.py defines test_all_clear_case twice (lines 71 and 92), the second shadows the first, 8 methods but only 7 tests run -- delete the dead copy; (d) test_capability_blocked_agent asserts first_blocking_gate=='agent_can_take_task', leaving gate 1 agent_auto_dispatch_block_reason with zero coverage even though it is the gate that fires for all 8 agents live. VERIFIED PASSING, no rework needed: read-only confirmed (git status unchanged after two live runs, no lock taken, state.get('seen_event_keys',{}) correctly avoids supervisor's setdefault mutation); forbidden files untouched (diff is only scripts/explain_dispatch.py, .orchestrator/test_explain_dispatch.py, task brief -- poll_workers/process_queue/reconcile_queue_records clean); all 7 named test cases present and 'python3 .orchestrator/test_explain_dispatch.py' is green; gate order for the 8 named functions matches dispatch_ready_tasks, and moving catalog-lock/dependencies to helper-notes is correct since supervisor evaluates them only on the helper-claim path. SUPERVISOR FYI, not an owner fault: acceptance #1 cites docs/04/supervisor_dispatch_refactor_proposal_2026-08-04.md, which does not exist on this branch, on dev, or anywhere in git history.
